findings.title: Heap buffer overflow in absl hash containers
findings.cvss40_note: CNA (Google) CVSS 4.0 score is 5.9 Medium (CVSS:4.0/AV:A/AC:H/AT:P/PR:L/UI:A/...); NVD CVSS 3.1 is 9.8 Critical. This register ranks on NVD CVSS 3.1, as for all other findings.
findings.fixed_version_source: SUSE backported fix commit 5a0e2cb5 to the 20230802 line as 20230802.3; upstream fix commit 5a0e2cb5e3958dd90bb8569a2766622cb74d90c1 is in release 20250127.0.
findings.reachability_text: AFFECTED VERSION. The flaw needs a caller to pass a huge size to the sized constructors / reserve() / rehash() of absl::{flat,node}hash{set,map}. Zero direct uses of absl::flat_hash* in postfiatd src/ and include/ (grep, pinned tree). abseil is used transitively by grpc; no attacker-controlled size argument was identified in grpc's internal use. Network reachability not demonstrated.
findings.description: Sized constructors, reserve() and rehash() of absl::{flat,node}hash{set,map} did not impose an upper bound on their size argument; a very large size causes an integer overflow when computing the container backing-store size and a subsequent out-of-bounds memory write.

findings.title: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset (CISA KEV, exploited in the wild)
findings.fixed_version_source: SUSE-SU-2024:0573-1: fixed in grpc 1.59.2; OSV GIT range [0, fix commit 06021d91).
findings.reachability_text: REACHABLE via the gRPC service. postfiatd's gRPC server is an HTTP/2 server (src/xrpld/app/main/GRPCServer.cpp:571-572, InsecureServerCredentials). Shipped configs bind [port_grpc] port 50051 on 127.0.0.1 (cfg/postfiatd-example.cfg:1466-1468); the bind address is operator-configurable, so exposure becomes remote if bound publicly. A remote unauthenticated attacker that can reach the endpoint can exhaust server resources with RST_STREAM floods.
findings.description: HTTP/2 Rapid Reset: a peer can send RST_STREAM frames immediately after requests, causing the server to do work that is then cancelled, enabling unauthenticated denial of service. Listed in CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities; exploited in the wild Aug-Oct 2023.

findings.title: HPACK table accounting error allows DoS via unwanted disconnects
findings.fixed_version_source: GHSA-496j-2rq6-j6cc ECOSYSTEM range starts at 0, fixed in 1.53.2 (pre-1.53 line).
findings.reachability_text: REACHABLE via the gRPC service (same endpoint as CVE-2023-44487): errors in HPACK table accounting cause unwanted disconnects between clients and servers; a remote peer can trigger it with crafted HEADERS frames.
findings.description: Errors in HPACK table accounting in gRPC C-core can lead to unwanted disconnects between clients and servers (denial of service).

findings.title: RAR5 infinite-loop denial of service
findings.cvss31_note: Vector not present in the fetched OSV record; score 7.5 as published (OpenCVE/NVD).
findings.fixed_version_source: Debian libarchive (3.8.6-1) changelog: 'Fix CVE-2026-4111'; Yocto: 'fixed since 3.8.6'; SUSE 3.8.6 changelog: 'RAR5 reader: fix infinite loop in rar5 decompression'.
findings.reachability_text: NOT REACHABLE via postfiatd's use. The only libarchive consumer in the tree is extractTarLz4 (src/libxrpl/basics/Archive.cpp:36-116), which enables ONLY archive_read_support_format_tar + lz4 filter. The RAR5 reader is never enabled.
findings.description: Logical deadlock between the RAR5 filter subsystem and the half-window output limiter leads to an infinite loop (DoS) on a crafted RAR5 archive.

findings.title: RAR heap out-of-bounds read (LZSS window)
findings.fixed_version_source: Debian libarchive (3.8.7-1) changelog: 'Fix CVE-2026-4424'; Yocto: 'fixed since 3.8.7'; SUSE 3.8.1 spec applies CVE-2026-4424.patch (3.8.1 affected).
findings.reachability_text: NOT REACHABLE via postfiatd's use: RAR reader never enabled (Archive.cpp enables tar only).
findings.description: Heap out-of-bounds read in the RAR archive processing logic due to improperly sized LZSS windows (archive_read_support_format_rar.c).

findings.title: zisofs block-pointer integer overflow (32-bit only)
findings.fixed_version_source: Debian libarchive (3.8.7-1) changelog: 'Fix CVE-2026-5121'; Yocto: 'fixed since 3.8.7'.
findings.reachability_text: NOT REACHABLE via postfiatd's use on two counts: the zisofs decompression code lives in the ISO9660 format reader (archive_read_support_format_iso9660.c), which Archive.cpp never enables; and the flaw triggers only on 32-bit systems, while the Dockerfile builds on 64-bit ubuntu:24.04.
findings.description: On 32-bit systems, an integer overflow in the zisofs block pointer allocation allows a heap overflow via a crafted ISO image.

findings.title: RAR5 reader double free
findings.fixed_version_source: Debian libarchive (3.8.8-1) changelog: 'Fix CVE-2026-14164'; Ubuntu 3.8.5-1ubuntu2.2 backports the fix to archive_read_support_format_rar5.c.
findings.reachability_text: NOT REACHABLE via postfiatd's use: RAR5 reader never enabled (Archive.cpp enables tar only).
findings.description: Double free in libarchive's RAR5 reader during parsing of a specially crafted RAR5 archive (dangling pointers in init_unpack).

findings.title: OpenSSL 1.1.1 end-of-life: no public security fixes since 2023-09-11
findings.fixed_version_source: OpenSSL project: 1.1.1 EOL 2023-09-11; 1.1.1w (2023-09-11) was the final 1.1.1 release.
findings.reachability_text: Support-status finding, not a single CVE. 1.1.1w is the final 1.1.1 release; any vulnerability discovered in the 1.1.1 line after 2023-09-11 receives no public fix. The pinned tree also blocks migration: src/libxrpl/crypto/digest.cpp uses RIPEMD160 low-level APIs removed from the OpenSSL 3.x default provider, so an upgrade needs code changes, not just a version bump (see decision memo).
findings.description: OpenSSL 1.1.1 reached end of life on 2023-09-11. The pinned version 1.1.1w is the last 1.1.1 release and receives no further public security fixes.

findings.title: zisofs decompression undefined behaviour
findings.fixed_version_source: Debian libarchive (3.8.7-1) changelog: 'Fix CVE-2026-4426'; Yocto: 'fixed since 3.8.7'; SUSE 3.8.1 spec applies CVE-2026-4426.patch.
findings.reachability_text: NOT REACHABLE via postfiatd's use: zisofs code lives in the ISO9660 format reader, never enabled by Archive.cpp.
findings.description: Undefined behaviour due to an unvalidated operand in a shift expression of the zisofs decompression code.

findings.title: NULL pointer dereference in ACL text parsing
findings.fixed_version_source: Debian libarchive (3.8.8-1) changelog: 'Fix CVE-2026-5745'; Ubuntu 3.8.5-1ubuntu2.2 backports the fix to archive_acl.c (archive_acl_from_text_nl).
findings.reachability_text: LATENT tar-path flaw. The vulnerable function archive_acl_from_text_nl() parses ACL text from tar PAX extended headers, and Archive.cpp enables tar reading with ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_ACL (Archive.cpp:75-77). BUT extractTarLz4 is the only function in Archive.cpp and has NO caller in src/ or include/ in the pinned tree (grep, 2026-11-26), so the code path is present in libxrpl source with no in-tree execution path in xrpld as pinned. Reachable only if the utility is invoked by downstream tooling or future code.
findings.description: NULL pointer dereference in the ACL parsing logic (archive_acl_from_text_nl) when processing a malformed ACL string in a tar archive.

findings.title: Heap overflow parsing tar PAX SUN.holesdata sparse attribute
findings.fixed_version_source: Debian libarchive (3.8.9-1) changelog: 'Fix CVE-2026-15028'; Ubuntu 3.8.5-1ubuntu2.2 backports the fix to archive_read_support_format_tar.c (1-byte OOB read).
findings.reachability_text: LATENT tar-path flaw. The vulnerable code is the tar reader's PAX extended-header parsing, which Archive.cpp enables (format tar). BUT extractTarLz4 has NO caller in src/ or include/ in the pinned tree, so the code path is present in libxrpl source with no in-tree execution path in xrpld as pinned. Reachable only if the utility is invoked; the input would then be an operator-supplied local tar file (CVSS AV:L/UI:R matches: local access + user interaction).
findings.description: A remote attacker can trigger a heap overflow by providing a specially crafted tar archive; the issue occurs during parsing of a PAX extended header containing a malformed SUN.holesdata sparse-file attribute (CWE-805/CWE-122).

findings.title: Signed integer overflow in ZIP writer (encrypted entries)
findings.fixed_version_source: Debian libarchive (3.8.9-1) changelog: 'Fix CVE-2026-16517'; Ubuntu 3.8.5-1ubuntu2.3: integer overflow in ZIP writer.
findings.reachability_text: NOT REACHABLE via postfiatd's use: the flaw is in the ZIP writer (archive_write_set_format_zip.c) with ZIP encryption enabled. Archive.cpp uses archive_write_disk only; it never writes zip.
findings.description: Signed integer overflow in archive_write_zip_header when ZIP encryption is enabled and the entry filename is crafted.

findings.title: strcpy heap overflow in gzip writer
findings.cvss31_note: Vector not present in the fetched OSV record; score 2.5 as published by GHSA-92wx-p669-8gr9.
findings.fixed_version_source: GHSA-92wx-p669-8gr9: 'libarchive 3.8.x before 3.8.2'; SUSE 3.8.2 changelog lists the gzip-writer fix.
findings.reachability_text: NOT REACHABLE via postfiatd's use: the flaw is in the gzip writer. Archive.cpp writes with archive_write_disk only and enables only the lz4 read filter; it never writes gzip.
findings.description: strcpy heap overflow in the gzip writer of libarchive 3.8.x.
